recent.title: Google Cloud Storage write errors in us-central1 last about 12.5 hours
recent.impact: From 11:00 UTC to 23:30 UTC on October 8, 2026, Cloud Storage upload and write operations in us-central1 saw elevated latency and error rates, and a smaller share of reads was slow or failing. Google gave a preliminary cause: a traffic sorting optimization meant to ease localized capacity shortfalls exhausted resources on specific backend storage nodes, with a separate database service issue adding metadata errors for part of the window. A full root cause analysis was still pending.

source.label: Google Cloud — Service health incident

recent.title: Ransomware forces IDC Frontier to isolate its East Japan Region 1 data center
recent.impact: Unauthorized access began around 03:40 JST on October 7, 2026. IDC Frontier confirmed a third-party ransomware attack, then isolated and halted the East Japan Region 1 data center. Contracts tied to that region cover 495 companies and local governments, and some customers were told data recovery could be difficult. The intrusion method and whether data was stolen had not been disclosed.

source.label: BleepingComputer / ITmedia report on IDCF Cloud ransomware

recent.title: Azure gateway outage cuts ExpressRoute, VPN and Firewall connectivity across 18 regions
recent.location: Multi-region (18 Azure regions, incl. West US, North Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan West, South Africa North)
recent.impact: From 20:30 UTC on September 30 to about 02:15 UTC on October 1, 2026 (roughly 5 h 45 min), Azure ExpressRoute Gateway, VPN Gateway, Firewall, Application Gateway/WAF and Azure VMware Solution customers saw degraded or lost network connectivity. Microsoft's status history said the timing correlated with infrastructure operating system servicing activity, which was paused. No final post-incident review was available at the time of writing.

source.label: Microsoft — Azure status history

recent.title: West Java halts construction of BDx 640 MW CGK4 AI campus eight days after groundbreaking
recent.impact: On September 30, 2026, West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi ordered work stopped at BDx's CGK4 campus, which had broken ground on September 22. The governor said two permits had not been issued — the environmental impact assessment (AMDAL) and the building approval (PBG) — and raised public concerns about water use from the Jatiluhur reservoir, noise and wastewater. CGK4 is planned as a 640 MW, six-building campus with 845 MVA of grid supply from PLN; Building 1 (120 MW) was targeted for early 2027. Reporting did not include a BDx statement, and the length of the stoppage is not known.

source.label: TNGlobal — Indonesia's West Java asks Singapore's BDx to halt data center 1 week after groundbreaking

recent.title: Fire: STT Seoul 1 (Gasan-dong)
recent.impact: A fire believed to have started in a transformer in a UPS room was reported at 11:55 and extinguished by 15:13. STT GDC said an electrical component failed while new equipment was being tested in an environment separate from customer systems. 105 people were evacuated; the operator said customer systems and data center operations were not affected.

source.label: DatacenterDynamics — Fire at data center in Seoul, South Korea, sees 100 people evacuated

recent.title: Subsea cable faults between Australia and Singapore degrade Asia-Pacific capacity; Cloudflare reports congestion
recent.location: Perth–Singapore corridor, Indonesian waters off Anyer, Java
recent.impact: Indigo West and Indigo Central suffered electrical shunt faults near Perth on August 8–9, 2026, and the Australia-Singapore Cable (operated by Vocus) was severed in Indonesian waters off Anyer on September 4. Per Submarine Networks, the faults removed all direct low-latency Perth–Singapore paths (about 100 Tbps), pushing round-trip times from roughly 60 ms to 300–400 ms as traffic rerouted via Guam, Japan or the transpacific. Cloudflare's status page reported multiple subsea outages causing congestion between its Tokyo and Singapore data centers from September 21 at 02:20 UTC and a regional performance degradation in Asia-Pacific from September 23. Repair of ASC was awaiting the cable ship CS Lodbrog, with delays attributed to Indonesian permitting and security approvals.

source.label: Submarine Networks — Perth–Singapore subsea outages deep-dive

recent.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv data centers — BeMobile/UCloud and De Novo facilities targeted
recent.impact: Russian forces struck at least two commercial data center facilities in Kyiv within a five-day span in mid-September 2026. On September 15, an attack hit the BeMobile facility operated by UCloud; the company did not disclose the extent of physical damage but confirmed some hosted websites, including Ukraine's National Paralympic Committee site, were temporarily knocked offline and expected to be restored within hours. On September 17, a broader wave of missile and drone strikes damaged energy and telecommunications infrastructure across the capital and injured more than 20 people, according to Ukrainian officials. On September 19, Russia's TASS state news agency said strikes had hit De Novo, one of Ukraine's largest commercial data centers — a Tier III-compliant, 360-rack facility that hosts major Ukrainian banks and the country's largest Infrastructure-as-a-Service cloud platform. Russian officials characterized De Novo as supporting Ukrainian military data processing; De Novo describes itself publicly as a sovereign-cloud and AI provider serving mission-critical civilian and commercial systems. Neither company has published a full damage assessment or restoration timeline, and the extent of physical destruction at either site has not been independently verified.

source.label: DataCenterDynamics — Russia claims strikes on De Novo data center in Kyiv, Ukraine

recent.title: Salesforce global platform outage disrupts Hyperforce instances during Dreamforce
recent.location: Global — Hyperforce instances across multiple regions, including the US, Japan, India, the UK, France and Germany
recent.impact: On September 16, 2026 — the second day of Salesforce's own Dreamforce conference in San Francisco — a global outage hit hundreds of customer instances from roughly 08:30 to 19:20 UTC (about 10.5 hours). Salesforce said requests were stalling while waiting on a response from an internal legacy login service, which consumed available server resources and limited the platform's capacity to process incoming requests; first-party GovCloud environments were largely unaffected. Customers reported severe delays, intermittent errors and inability to access some services, including support-case creation and scheduled job execution. Salesforce rolled out region-by-region fixes, and some customers needed manual session resets or cache clears after the fix before declaring the incident resolved at 19:20 UTC.

source.label: The Register — Salesforce staggers back to feet after global outage

recent.title: Microsoft 365 sign-in failures lock users out worldwide
recent.location: Global, with concentrated user reports in the US and UK
recent.impact: Starting around 13:22 UTC on September 16, 2026, Microsoft tracked a spike in Microsoft 365 sign-in failures (incident MO1472904) accompanied by 5xx server errors on its authentication layer. Users with an already-active session could often keep working, but anyone forced through a fresh sign-in, token refresh, MFA prompt, portal session renewal or new-device enrollment could fail to authenticate. Microsoft said it was reviewing service telemetry and user reports to isolate the root cause and was checking whether upstream dependencies contributed; some affected customers saw service return as the review continued, but Microsoft had not published a confirmed root cause or final duration at last report. This is a separate, later incident from the larger Microsoft 365/Exchange Online authentication outage of August 31 – September 3, 2026 (IDs EX1464935/MO1465074).

source.label: Cyber Security News — Microsoft 365 hit by new outage as users report widespread 502 and 503 errors

recent.title: AWS confirms permanent customer data loss in Bahrain and UAE regions after Iran-linked strikes on facilities
recent.location: Middle East (Bahrain) region and Middle East (UAE) region, mec1-az2 availability zone
recent.impact: In a September 15, 2026 update to its Health Dashboard, AWS said damage from drone/missile strikes earlier in the year on facilities supporting its Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE) regions spanned multiple Availability Zones and "exceeded what our regional and multi-AZ services are designed to withstand." AWS concluded it cannot restore access to resources and data hosted exclusively in the Bahrain region, and reached the same conclusion for the mec1-az2 Availability Zone in the UAE region; work continues on remaining UAE zones (mec1-az1, mec1-az3). The permanent loss affects only customers whose sole data copy sat inside the damaged infrastructure — those with cross-region replication or backups elsewhere could rebuild — but AWS has not publicly quantified the number of affected customers or the volume of data lost. The episode is a rare confirmed case of physical destruction overwhelming cloud multi-AZ redundancy design assumptions.

source.label: Help Net Security — AWS Middle East outage: permanent data loss in Bahrain, UAE

recent.title: xAI Memphis compute center outage cascades into simultaneous ChatGPT, Claude and Grok disruptions
recent.location: Memphis, Tennessee, USA (xAI compute center), plus OpenAI and Anthropic serving infrastructure
recent.impact: Around 7:43am PT on September 3, 2026, three unrelated AI chat services — ChatGPT, Claude and Grok — went down within the same roughly 90-minute window, an anomaly given each is normally on a separate failure path. OpenAI told The Register that "a routing error" made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users starting at 7:43am PT. Separately, xAI said an outage at its Memphis, Tennessee compute center that morning took down Grok and also disrupted service for unspecified "compute partners," which xAI/SpaceX identified as including Anthropic; Anthropic's status page confirmed a 3-hour-6-minute partial outage with elevated error rates on Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API, restored by 16:16 UTC. Google's Gemini was unaffected throughout, since it runs on separate Google Cloud infrastructure. The episode illustrates how concentrated AI compute supply chains can turn one facility's outage into a multi-vendor incident.

source.label: The Register — ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all had outages at the same time

recent.title: Google Cloud: network degradation in us-central1-b takes down 15 products for up to 4h08m
recent.impact: On September 1, 2026, Google's own Service Health dashboard logged incident J5ia5t9p3g9Q5Wi7r8Ev: multiple products running in the us-central1-b zone experienced network service degradation. Affected services included Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Cloud Bigtable, Cloud Spanner, Cloud Run, App Engine, AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, Apigee, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Dataflow, Hybrid Connectivity, Looker and Virtual Private Cloud. Impact duration varied by product, from about 14 minutes for VPC to 4 hours 8 minutes for Cloud Run and App Engine. Google did not publish a root-cause explanation alongside the status update.

source.label: Google Cloud Service Health — incident summary

recent.title: Microsoft 365: authentication-configuration fault disrupts Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and Defender XDR for multiple days
recent.impact: Starting around 5:30pm UTC on August 31, 2026, Microsoft opened incident EX1464935 after users reported failed authentication, delayed mail delivery, broken mailbox search and admin-portal problems in Exchange Online. Microsoft's follow-up incident MO1465074 confirmed the disruption spread to Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft Graph, Purview, the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, Copilot and Defender XDR because the services share an authentication component. Microsoft identified the root cause as a fault in a core authentication configuration and rolled out a phased remediation. Mailbox connectivity returned to expected thresholds within about 24 hours, but search functionality and full recovery of Exchange Online, Universal Print, OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online remained impacted as of September 2, roughly 48 hours after the incident began.

source.label: Microsoft 365 Status (official) — incident update

recent.title: Proton: total cooling failure at Frankfurt datacenter takes down Mail, VPN, Drive and Pass for 2h18m
recent.impact: Between 00:09 and 02:27 CEST on August 27, 2026, nearly all Proton services — Mail, VPN, Calendar, Drive, Pass, SimpleLogin, Wallet and the Lumo assistant — became unreachable. Proton engineers identified the cause at 00:38 CEST as what CEO Andy Yen publicly described as an "unprecedented total cooling failure" at the company's Frankfurt datacenter, which required manual intervention and a shift of traffic to backup sites rather than automated failover. Recovery began around 01:37 CEST, with full resolution by 02:27 CEST. Yen stated that no user data was exposed, deleted or compromised, since the failure was physical and facility-level rather than a breach or software defect, and Proton's end-to-end encryption was unaffected.

source.label: Andy Yen (Proton CEO) — public incident statement

recent.title: Google Cloud us-west1 (Oregon) region: multi-service degradation for about 3h40m
recent.impact: From roughly 08:40 to 12:20 Pacific time on August 20, 2026, customers in Google Cloud's us-west1 region experienced timeouts, degraded service and elevated error rates across more than 20 products, including Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Dataflow, Cloud Run and IAM. Google's Service Health dashboard tracked the incident through mitigation and recovery; services outside us-west1 were not affected. Google had not published a detailed root-cause explanation as of this writing.

source.label: Google Cloud Service Health — incident report
